narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 52.8% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability tipped just above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was denied.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your class ranking in the third year of law school was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Placing in the second decile, noticeably below the average of roughly sixth-decile performance among accepted students, signaled to the model that you may struggle under the pressure of the bar exam. Your first-year ranking in the third decile, also well below the typical sixth-decile level of successful applicants, added further weight in the same direction.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.10 worked in the opposite direction. Although it is slightly below the 3.23 average of accepted students, the model still saw this as a modestly positive signal that slightly increased the chance you might pass. However, this encouraging factor was not strong enough to overcome the two clear academic-ranking concerns.

Given these results, you should focus on strengthening your academic trajectory and bar-exam readiness. Consider retaking key courses to improve your class standing, enrolling in a structured bar-preparation program, or gaining additional practical legal experience before reapplying. These steps can directly address the areas the model weighed most heavily. (218 words)
